### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **51** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**56** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 56 pages)`, `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 55 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **50** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f4c5473d045a2d84708e2b7b9e89ed79fda17889` — the merge of head `cc6754e708af478361640abaf6f0eff2b793b05d` into base `9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f4c5473d045a2d84708e2b7b9e89ed79fda17889 && git checkout f4c5473d045a2d84708e2b7b9e89ed79fda17889
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2 cc6754e708af478361640abaf6f0eff2b793b05d && git checkout -B drift-repro 9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2 && git merge --no-ff cc6754e708af478361640abaf6f0eff2b793b05d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9c29d732a191496cf2069da9419c251eaba557c2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

security#2 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj

The seat adopts the delta record below. The same isolated reviewer rendered it on this head at the contract-review tier, after a FAIL at `222a618930` that the seat holds privately. Under the maintainer's ruling, this PR lands rule items 1 and 2; item 3 is follow-up #35184.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cc6754e708af478361640abaf6f0eff2b793b05d`
Local-runs: probe — one throwaway worktree at the head, since removed, to run the seed and invitation suites and two ablations of the mark's trigger. The seed suites passed 20 and the invitation suites 108. Restoring the operator-class trigger turned exactly the new control red; removing the staging turned 6 red; each was restored. `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-empty-changeset` exit 0.
Scope: the delta `222a618930..cc6754e708` (one commit, 7 files, +83 −24), judged against the earlier findings, plus the replacement PR body. The head merges cleanly with main.

### ① Derived judgments

- **M1: closed.**
  - The mark is staged only when the request proved the development seed's own provisioning ticket (`auth-manager-membership-admission.ts:238, 324-331`). In shipped source, only the seed admin and `demoStaff` stage that ticket.
  - A real-pipeline control (`dev-seed-credential-production.test.ts:271-288`) pins the boundary. An account an administrator creates in development carries no mark and signs in outside development mode. Restoring the old trigger turns exactly that control red.
  - The code comments, changeset, docs and body now describe the mark as covering the seed's accounts only.
- **S1: closed.** "Not ended at boot" appears in the changeset and in `self-hosting.mdx:628-632`, at rule level.
- **S2: closed.** The text now states what the command checks, and that the deployment's own policy and history are not applied.
- **S3: closed.** One statement covers reset links and sessions, with the remedy: run with the server stopped, or restart it. A secondary storage kept outside the server process outlives a restart and is cleared by hand.
- **N1, N2: closed.**
- **N3: closed.** `/sign-in/phone-number` has a real-pipeline case. No username plugin is composed or routed, so the username path is unit-pinned as a guard.
- **No new over-refusal.** The delta narrows which accounts are marked and changes no refusal. The invitation suites pass unchanged.
- **PR body:** accurate against the diff.

**Findings at this head**

- **N4 (nit).** `self-hosting.mdx:628-632` uses release-note phrasing ("what this release refuses", "is follow-up #35184") on a standing docs page. Timeless wording would age better.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and correct:
- `patch` on the three packages, with `Metadata-protocol: none`;
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, listing both the widening and the narrowing;
- the BREAKING banner and `!`;
- the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, with its corrected reason.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No governed paths.
- `Clause-②: yes`: this at-tier record reviews the new exports and the CLI topic.
- Item 3 stays out of this PR, in #35184.
- The secondary-storage text follows option A of a maintainer question. If the answer is B, the head needs a new record.
- [detail held by the security seat]

### ④ Design judgment

Keying the mark on the proven ticket, not on a creation class, ties it to the one act that defines a seed credential. It cannot widen when a new operator-class method is added.
